ambiguities.text: The specification does not define the HTTP endpoint path or port for metrics exposure.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume standard Prometheus conventions apply: /metrics endpoint on a configurable port (commonly 9090 or similar).

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'ethereum_best_known_block_number' is described as 'estimated highest block available' without defining the estimation method.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume this derives from peer announcements during sync (highest block number reported by peers) or current height when synced.

ambiguities.text: The specification states clients 'may publish additional metrics' but does not define any guidance on naming conventions for these.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume additional metrics should use a client-specific prefix (e.g., geth_, besu_) to avoid namespace conflicts.

implicit_assumptions.description: The metrics endpoint is only accessible to authorized monitoring systems.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Attackers could gain operational intelligence about node state, sync status, and peer connectivity.

implicit_assumptions.description: All client implementations interpret the metric definitions identically.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Cross-client monitoring dashboards may display inconsistent or misleading data.

implicit_assumptions.description: The Prometheus server scraping metrics is a trusted monitoring system.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious actors could use metrics to time attacks based on sync state or peer count.
